findings.rootCause: The LMDB pipeline's request-bound rewrites embed committed-store facts before Cascades runs: LmdbFilterSimplifierOptimizer.exactStoredTermFilterAnchor replaces FILTER(?o = c) with a VALUES anchor enumerating the COMPLETE committed stored terms value-equal to c (true only for the planning data revision), and materializedSmallLiteralFilterAnchor drops/exactifies the filter on the strength of the predicate's object-domain guarantee (true only while that guarantee keeps its contents). LmdbPipelinePlanCache.publishDecision stripped the only hard identity (PredicateRangeIdentity) unless the PACKED summary declared PREDICATE_RANGE_DATA (a packed rule proof; pipeline rewrites never set it) and the data revision existed only in the soft EvidenceSnapshot, so LmdbPlanDecisionCache.lookupVersion answered UseAndRefresh('outside-stability-envelope') after any commit and served the anchored plan; LmdbDetachedPlanRefresh replanned the already-rewritten prepared source (anchor included) and its ensureSemanticsCurrent compared only predicateRangeVersion, a schema hash (encoding + exclusion config + flags) that no commit changes, so the refresh republished the stale anchor permanently. Two latent gaps found by the critique made a naive hard dependency unusable: (a) SemanticDependencies had one index dimension (indexGeneration/indexIdentity) so a contents-only tier could not coexist with a data-revision tier on lookup; (b) publishBuild refuses to replace a VALID family version and nothing marked HARD_INVALID on a mismatch (hardInvalid only via markEvidenceChanged, no production caller), so a hard mismatch would replan on every invocation forever.
findings.change: Roadmap 4.2 rewrite certificates, scoped to the caches. (1) New LmdbPlanAssumptions record (committedSnapshotDependent, guaranteePredicates) with dedicated planned metrics optimizer.planAssumption.committedSnapshot / optimizer.planAssumption.guaranteePredicate; LmdbFilterSimplifierOptimizer stamps the first exactly at the exact stored-term anchor (:455) and the second only where a guarantee decided the drop/expansion (consumedGuaranteePredicate mirrors canMaterializeSmallLiteralFilterAnchor/expandFiniteAnchor; the OPTIONAL safe-values shortcut with nothing to expand is not stamped), never derived from OPTIMIZER_GUARANTEE_ANCHOR_PREDICATE (critique minor). LmdbQueryOptimizerPipeline.computePlan collects the assumptions from the pre-Cascades tree (PackedPlanMaterializer does not carry source metrics), annotates the plan (optimizer.planAssumptions, explain-visible) and passes them into PlanComputation and LmdbDetachedPlanRefresh. (2) Two-tier hard dependencies (critique major #1): SemanticDependencies gains dataRevision/dataRevisionDependent next to indexGeneration/indexIdentity/indexGenerationDependent; the lookup side always supplies both (semanticDependencies(context) with dataRevision = planning data revision, dependent=true, identity = PredicateRangeIdentity); publishDecision narrows per assumptions via hardDependencies(): committedSnapshot -> keep the data-revision tier (any commit -> replan), guarantee-dependent (assumption or packed PREDICATE_RANGE_DATA) -> keep the identity tier (contents-only, indexGeneration 0L as before, commits that leave the guarantee unchanged still USE/USE_AND_REFRESH), neither -> both stripped (today's use-and-refresh). matchesCurrent compares only the declared tiers. RefreshComputation/RefreshPublication/publishRefresh mirror the fields so refreshed versions keep the hard dependency. (3) Publication after a mismatch (critique major #2): lookupVersion CASes the family version to hardInvalid (and re-points aliases) before returning replan('semantic-dependency-mismatch'), so publishBuild accepts the plan built for the current dependencies and the third run is a cache hit (asserted e2e: afterCommitPlan pipelinePlanCacheHit=true, USE). (4) LmdbDetachedPlanRefresh carries the assumptions, the build data revision and the build PredicateRangeIdentity; ensureAssumptionsCurrent refuses (before opening a planning snapshot, and again after planning) when committedSnapshotDependent && dataRevision != build revision or when a consumed guarantee's identity changed; predicateRangeDependent = packed summary || guarantee assumption; the refreshed FamilyVersion keeps the same hard tiers. (5) predicateRangeVersion is documented as the guarantee SCHEMA version (LmdbEstimatorStorageAccess, TripleStore.effectiveRdfTermDomainsVersion); guarantee CONTENTS are keyed through PredicateRangeIdentity (pipeline decision cache) and, for the packed cache, through Context.dataRevision (a contents change is a commit) plus b2's sameQueryContext predicateRangeVersion check. Commit-visibility vs revision-bump ordering (critique blocker for this batch): analysed and documented in LmdbPipelinePlanCache.getOrComputePlan -- the pipeline captures context.revision() before planning and publishes only if it equals the revision re-read after planning; the exact-probe caches (b2) and LmdbDetachedPlanRefresh bracket their reads the same way; with TripleStore publishing the revision only after the readers were reset (b2), a plan/probe can never be keyed under a revision newer than the data it enumerated, and the residual 'newer data under the captured revision' case is either caught by the re-check or keyed under a revision no later lookup uses. Deviation from the task wording, following the design: the detached refresh still starts from the prepared (rewritten) source; re-running the request-bound optimizers inside the detached refresh would require it to retain the pipeline/estimator/strategy it is contractually forbidden to retain and is a plan-quality item, not a correctness one, once a refresh cannot run on stale assumptions (detachedRefreshMustNotReplanFromStaleAnchoredPreparedSource is green: the refresh is refused and the synchronous replan re-runs the rewrites against current data).

crossWpNotes: wp1 (LmdbFilterSimplifierOptimizer): every new anchor/drop path that consumes committed stored terms or a guarantee must call LmdbPlanAssumptions.stampCommittedSnapshot / stampGuaranteePredicate on the node it creates, otherwise the pipeline decision cache treats the plan as data-independent (use-and-refresh across commits).

wp5 (Frontier lifecycle): flaky IOException 'Frontier mutation journal no longer retains all mutations after sequence 3' from TripleStore.readFrontierMutationsAfter via LmdbSailStore.appendCurrentFrontierMutationTail during a SNAPSHOT reader's commit flush after a concurrent writer commit (LmdbPlanCacheCommitInvalidationTest.snapshotTransactionMustNotUseAnchorsProbedFromNewerCommit, 1 of 3 runs); the frontierMutationTailSequence bookkeeping does not tolerate the journal being acknowledged/pruned past the tail between commits.

wp2/wp7 (packed rules): a packed EmptySet proof from range facts already declares PREDICATE_RANGE_DATA and is now published on the guarantee identity tier; any future packed proof that consumes an exact committed-data fact (e.g. bounded exact-zero FilterEvidence turned into an EmptySet alternative) must declare a summary dependency the pipeline can map to the data-revision tier (LmdbPipelinePlanCache.hardDependencies).

3.3.3/3.5 ordering (critique): TripleStore keeps publishing the data revision AFTER txnManager.reset(); with the capture-before/re-check-after bracketing in LmdbPipelinePlanCache, LmdbFilterSelectivityStats probe caches and LmdbDetachedPlanRefresh this is the safe order (old data can never be keyed under a new revision); moving the bump before the reset would create exactly that poisoning. Documented in LmdbPipelinePlanCache.getOrComputePlan.

b2 (3.3.3/3.3.4/3.8.4/3.3.5) lmdb post-fix runs were never observed by the b2 agent (killed during install); they were observed green in this batch's first run (LmdbDataRevisionRestartTest 6/6 after updating one outdated expectation, LmdbExactProbeCacheDataRevisionTest 6/6, LmdbCascadesPlanningFailSafeTest 1/1, LmdbPipelinePlanCacheFailedFlightTest 1/1, LmdbPackedFamilyFlightIsolationTest 3/3, LmdbExactFilterProbeCacheTest 4/4) -- see '## b2 post-fix (lmdb selection ...)' in the evidence file.
followUps: Plan-quality follow-up (design 'deferred option'): make the detached refresh start from the pre-rewrite source by re-running the request-bound optimizers against the detached planning snapshot inside LmdbDetachedPlanRefresh; today a refresh whose assumptions went stale is refused and the family is replaced by a synchronous replan.

LmdbPlanDecisionCache.markEvidenceChanged/hardInvalid still has no production caller besides the new lookup-side retirement; a store-side hook (e.g. on predicate-guarantee rebuild) could retire dependent families eagerly instead of on first lookup.
Consider a metric/counter for hard-dependency replans (semantic-dependency-mismatch) so benchmark runs can see how often FILTER-anchored shapes replan after commits.
